solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Alarm for pilot when landing gear's out of order

indicators.note: something out of order is jumbled up, so these letters are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A pilot's warning light comes on because the undercarriage has failed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' rearranges LANDING GEARS, ignoring the apostrophe, into the twelve letters of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A warning that something is wrong, such as a cockpit alert, is exactly this kind of signal.

clue.text: Looks like a soft fruit

parts.note: P is short for piano, the musical direction for soft
pears are a fruit

explanation.surface: Something resembles a squashy piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looks like' reads as one phrase, but 'Looks' alone is the definition and 'like' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To look a certain way is to seem or give that impression, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Unfortunate groom without love — or brains!

definitions.text: Unfortunate groom without love — or brains!

indicators.note: unfortunate here suggests things gone wrong, so the remaining letters are jumbled
without tells us to take the letter for love out of the groom

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
the dash is read as a minus sign, and minus means less

explanation.surface: A hapless bridegroom lacks both affection and intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes one O (love) from GROOM, leaving GROM, which 'Unfortunate' rearranges as GORM; the dash, read as a minus sign, gives LESS. The whole clue describes someone brainless.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stupid or lacking sense is described by this British informal adjective.

clue.text: Currency starts to recover after near disaster

indicators.note: starts to points at the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A national currency begins to bounce back after narrowly avoiding collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the monetary unit of South Africa, so it is an example of a currency.

clue.text: Facing death I then get mostly careless

parts.note: then, as in 'and after that', means next

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: remiss means careless or negligent

explanation.surface: Someone at death's door admits to growing reckless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims REMISS to REMIS; 'get' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase is used of someone in an extreme situation, especially at the point of dying.

clue.text: One version shows us when pigs fly

indicators.note: shows us means the letters are on display inside the phrase that comes before

explanation.surface: One telling of an old saying offers the time when pigs take wing.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across the words: oNE VERsion.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom about flying pigs describes an event that will not happen at any time.

clue.text: Lie around on certain days off

indicators.note: around suggests the letters of the word are turned about into a new order

parts.note: certain means sure

explanation.surface: Someone lounges about on their regular rest days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lie around' looks like the definition of lounging; 'Lie' is fodder and 'around' its anagram signal, with 'on' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Free time away from work is what days off provide, a near synonym.

clue.text: Do, before leaving work finally

parts.note: a do is a party, and one held as someone leaves a job for the last time is a send-off celebration

explanation.surface: Instructions to complete a task before finishing for the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like a verb, an order to get something done; it is the noun for a social gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A send-off celebration for someone retiring or leaving a job is held under this name.

clue.text: Dangerous antagonists must trouble a beautician

definitions.meaning: people who are threatening and hard to deal with
taken literally, clients who are unattractive would challenge someone whose job is making people look good

explanation.surface: Thugs are bound to give a beauty therapist problems.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names nasty, threatening people, while literally it means plain-looking clients.

clue.text: Hopeful reduction in supply of drug

indicators.note: reduction tells us the word is cut down by losing its final letter

parts.note: someone hopeful is aspiring

explanation.surface: An optimistic cut in the supply of a medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduction' drops the last G from ASPIRING; 'in supply of' joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This common painkiller, acetylsalicylic acid, is an everyday example of a drug.

clue.text: Showing one's green?

parts.note: green is the colour of jealousy, so displaying it means feeling jealous of someone

explanation.surface: Displaying one's inexperience or eco-credentials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' suggests naivety or the environment; here it is the 'green-eyed monster' of jealousy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being jealous of another's possessions or luck is the green feeling shown here.

clue.text: Send message via Englishman, say

indicators.note: say tells us the pieces are to be spoken and heard, not spelt

parts.note: E for English plus MALE for man

explanation.surface: A request to pass a message through a man from England.
explanation.walkthrough: E (English) and MALE (man) said together match the answer; 'via' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To send a message electronically is the verb sense of this word.

clue.text: "Ray-burst" transforms a sparkling gem

indicators.note: transforms means the letters are changed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A burst of light turns a jewel into something glittering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transforms' rearranges RAYBURST, ignoring the hyphen.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a red gemstone showing a six-rayed star effect, so it is a kind of jewel.

clue.text: Two-part harmony request MPs often hear

indicators.note: two-part means the word is given twice, side by side

parts.note: harmony means order, as in peace and order

explanation.surface: A singer asks for two-part harmony, a request politicians hear in parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: The Speaker of the UK House of Commons calls this to restore quiet among MPs (Members of Parliament).
explanation.definitionFit: The cry used by the Commons Speaker to call rowdy members to quiet is this repeated word.

clue.text: Financial security the simple way

definitions.meaning: a comfortable life free from money worries
literally, a road that is easy

explanation.surface: Money safety achieved by the uncomplicated route.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a life of comfort and wealth, and literally an easy road.

clue.text: List of people in the top class

parts.note: people can mean men
U stands for upper class in British usage

explanation.surface: A register of people in the highest class.
explanation.walkthrough: U meaning upper class comes from Nancy Mitford's 'U and non-U' labels; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill of fare is a list of dishes, and computer options also come in such a list.

clue.text: Explain in detail, by writing letters?

definitions.meaning: literally, saying a word one character at a time

explanation.surface: Clarify fully, perhaps through correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to make plain, and literally to give a word letter by letter.

clue.text: Sort of poisoning empty pub might indicate

definitions.meaning: a toxic condition caused by a heavy metal once used in paint and pipes
taking out the middle of pub leaves PB, the chemical symbol for this metal

explanation.surface: A deserted bar may hint at a kind of toxic contamination.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition works through chemistry: P and B, the outsides of pub, form the symbol Pb.
explanation.definitionFit: This toxic heavy metal gives its name to a well-known form of poisoning.

clue.text: They stress a dollar's value …

parts.note: a dollar is worth a hundred cents, C being the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Banks emphasise what a dollar is worth.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links into the next clue's surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Marks of emphasis on syllables or letters are stresses in speech.

clue.text: In fine tapestry it appears in favourite place

indicators.note: appears in tells us the small word turns up inside the other pieces

parts.note: a favourite is a pet
a point is a place, as in a point on the map

explanation.surface: A small word turns up in a well-loved spot in some delicate needlework.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'In' is a link word, not a container signal; the blog notes the enumeration might better read (5,5).
explanation.definitionFit: This is embroidery worked in very small diagonal stitches on canvas, a fine needlework.

clue.text: … including one's gold tooth!

parts.note: inc is the abbreviation for including
I for one, plus 'S
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: and a gold tooth too!
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins the surface to the previous clue's dollar.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a front cutting tooth, so a particular kind of tooth.

clue.text: Ascent or, bizarrely, descent comes from one

indicators.note: bizarrely suggests the letters are in a strange order and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Going up, or oddly enough down, originates from one source.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ascent' and 'descent' look like a pair of opposites; one is fodder, the other part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A forebear is the person from whom a family line descends.

clue.text: Sainthood's gloomy expression

parts.note: the first part of the word, saint, abbreviates to S
the second part of the word, hood, is a cowl, as worn by a monk

explanation.surface: A holy person's sombre look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sainthood' reads as one word but splits as Saint plus hood.
explanation.definitionFit: A frown of anger or displeasure is a dark look on the face.

clue.text: Not well treated by this deputy?

definitions.text: Not well treated by this deputy?

parts.words: Not well treated by this deputy?
parts.note: it reads as poor treatment, but means sick patients seen by a stand-in doctor

explanation.surface: Someone complains of being badly handled by a stand-in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not well treated' suggests bad treatment; it means people who are not well being treated.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor or cleric standing in temporarily for another is called this.

clue.text: Land of Isaiah, perhaps, without borders

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged another way
without borders means the outer letters of the name are removed

explanation.surface: The prophet's homeland, maybe, with no frontiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without borders' leaves SAIA, which 'perhaps' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: This continent is a great landmass, so loosely a land.

clue.text: Juliet's last embrace means so much more

indicators.note: last points at the final letter of the name

parts.note: to embrace is to enfold

explanation.surface: Juliet's final hug means far more than anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'means' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Multiplied by ten is a great deal greater, hence a large increase.

clue.text: Poles stuck in trail for support

indicators.note: stuck in means one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: spoor is the track or trail of an animal
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Polish people get bogged down on a path while seeking help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' suggests people from Poland; it is the two compass poles.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a person or event financially is to support them.

clue.text: Energy supplier, almost alone, takes a right beating

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word is lost

parts.note: alone means sole
battery is a beating, as in assault and battery

explanation.surface: A power provider, nearly on its own, takes a thrashing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims SOLE to SOL; 'takes' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A cell that turns sunlight into stored electric power supplies energy.
